Here is a Python script to fetch the last June 2023 revision for the August day pages and parse references:

import requests
import re

SESSION = requests.Session()
API = "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php"
pages = [f"August {i}" for i in range(1, 32)]

TWITTER_RE = re.compile(r"https?://(?:www\.)?(?:twitter\.com|x\.com)/[^/]+/status/\d+")
ARCHIVE_RE = re.compile(r"https?://web\.archive\.org/web/\d+/(https?://(?:www\.)?(?:twitter\.com|x\.com)/[^/]+/status/\d+)")


def get_revision_content(title):
    params = {
        "action": "query",
        "prop": "revisions",
        "titles": title,
        "rvlimit": 1,
        "rvdir": "older",
        "rvstart": "2023-06-30T23:59:59Z",
        "rvprop": "ids|timestamp|content|slots",
        "rvslots": "main",
        "format": "json"
    }
    r = SESSION.get(API, params=params)
    r.raise_for_status()
    data = r.json()
    pages_dict = data.get("query", {}).get("pages", {})
    for _, p in pages_dict.items():
        revs = p.get("revisions")
        if revs:
            # new content model keeps slots
            slot = revs[0].get("slots", {}).get("main", {})
            return slot.get("content")
    return ""


def count_twitter_refs(text):
    count = 0
    # direct twitter/x post URLs
    count += len(TWITTER_RE.findall(text or ""))
    # archived twitter/x post URLs
    count += len(ARCHIVE_RE.findall(text or ""))
    return count


total = 0
per_page = {}
for title in pages:
    content = get_revision_content(title)
    c = count_twitter_refs(content)
    per_page[title] = c
    total += c

print("Per-page counts:", per_page)
print("Total:", total)
